title: macOS Filesystem Capacity from Splunk TA df
exclusions: Monitors one explicitly governed writable macOS mount per enrolled host from complete `Splunk_TA_nix` `df.sh` events. For current macOS boot-volume groups this is normally `/System/Volumes/Data`; `/` is valid only when the host policy and same-host validation establish that it is the intended writable volume. It does not calculate total APFS-container allocation, add the used values of APFS sibling volumes, distinguish free from purgeable space, guarantee that Finder, Storage settings, Disk Utility, and `df` show the same available value, measure per-user quotas, discover large files, forecast growth, monitor unmounted volumes, prove expected-host coverage, or remediate low capacity. APFS volumes in one container share free space, while `df` capacity is reported for a particular filesystem; therefore the result must not be labeled whole-disk or container utilization. The search ignores hosts without a valid enabled policy and rejects missing, stale, malformed, out-of-range, or unit-unparseable samples. It applies no maintenance suppression, does not certify update readiness or hardware health, and provides no security or regulatory attestation.
evidence: After deployment, retain the version-controlled `macos_filesystem_capacity_from_splunk_ta_df` saved-search definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch and triggered-result history; the exact `macos_df_capacity_policy.csv` revision; effective `Splunk_TA_nix` `df.sh` input and search-time configuration; add-on, forwarder, macOS, APFS, and Splunk platform versions; expected-host/source-health and policy-health reports; and dated positive/negative controls. Each finding should preserve `_time`, `host`, `Filesystem`, `Type`, `MountedOn`, raw `Size`/`Used`/`Avail`/`UsePct`, normalized `used_pct`, exact `available_bytes`, displayed GiB, thresholds, severity, owner, and runbook. For an incident retain contemporaneous `/bin/df -h <expected_mount>`, Disk Utility or System Settings storage observations, relevant APFS container/volume context, policy disposition, and any bounded suppression. These artifacts show what the configured collector and rule reported at recorded times; this documentation-only review created no macOS or Splunk runtime evidence and does not prove continuous collection, exact purgeable capacity, update eligibility, or root cause.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index with the add-on's `df` search-time knowledge, add an enabled policy for `host=mac-cap-positive`, `expected_mount=/System/Volumes/Data`, warning/critical used thresholds `90/95`, warning/critical free-byte thresholds `42949672960/21474836480`, and a current review date. Ingest three fresh complete `source=df sourcetype=df` samples separately and run a fixed-time copy of the SPL: (1) `UsePct=90%`, `Avail=50Gi` must return warning by the inclusive percentage boundary; (2) `UsePct=70%`, `Avail=20Gi` must return critical by the inclusive free-byte boundary; (3) `UsePct=96%`, `Avail=30Gi` must return critical by percentage. Assert `available_bytes` is respectively 53687091200, 21474836480, and 32212254720, proving that `Gi` uses powers of 1024 rather than decimal gigabytes.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Using the same isolated contract, ingest a newest fresh row with `MountedOn=/System/Volumes/Data`, `UsePct=89%`, and `Avail=41Gi`; expect zero findings. Then test each guard independently and expect zero primary rows: a root `/` row when policy expects the Data mount; a Linux or unlisted host with no policy; `enabled=0`; warning used percentage greater than or equal to critical; critical free bytes greater than or equal to warning free bytes; `UsePct=?`; `UsePct=101%`; `Avail=?`; a sample 901 seconds old; and a future sample. Verify separate source/policy-health searches report missing expected hosts, stale or rejected events, duplicate policy keys, and invalid policy rather than allowing silence to appear healthy.

dataSources: Complete tabular events from the `df.sh` scripted event input supplied by Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (`Splunk_TA_nix`, Splunkbase 833), collected on managed Macs by a Splunk Universal Forwarder and routed by local convention to `index=os`, `source=df`, `sourcetype=df`. Splunk documents `df.sh` as the mounted-volume free-space collector and currently lists it as supported on the documented macOS cohorts. The required event fields are `_time`, `host`, `Filesystem`, `Type`, `Size`, `Used`, `Avail`, `UsePct`, and `MountedOn`; the add-on also supplies CIM Performance/Storage aliases when its search-time knowledge is installed. `Size`, `Used`, and `Avail` are display values emitted from the platform command, not fields named or guaranteed to be kilobytes. The SPL parses `Avail` suffixes explicitly and treats an unsuffixed value according to the add-on's historical one-KiB-block convention. A governed CSV maps each enrolled Mac to exactly one expected writable mount and local thresholds.
app: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (`Splunk_TA_nix`, Splunkbase 833) installed on the macOS Universal Forwarder collection tier and on Splunk tiers that require its parsing/search-time knowledge. The Universal Forwarder is a Splunk product download, not Splunkbase app 617; `df.sh` is a scripted input, not a modular input or HEC poll.

spl:
index=os source=df sourcetype=df host=* earliest=-20m@m latest=-2m@m
| eval mounted_on=coalesce(MountedOn,mount), used_pct=tonumber(rtrim(tostring(coalesce(UsePct,Capacity,PercentUsedSpace,storage_used_percent)),"%")), size_display=tostring(Size), used_display=tostring(Used), available_display=upper(trim(tostring(Avail)))
| rex field=available_display "^(?<available_number>[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)(?<available_unit>B|K|KB|KI|KIB|M|MB|MI|MIB|G|GB|GI|GIB|T|TB|TI|TIB|P|PB|PI|PIB)?$"
| eval available_number=tonumber(available_number), available_multiplier=case(available_unit="B",1,isnull(available_unit) OR available_unit="",1024,in(available_unit,"K","KB","KI","KIB"),1024,in(available_unit,"M","MB","MI","MIB"),1048576,in(available_unit,"G","GB","GI","GIB"),1073741824,in(available_unit,"T","TB","TI","TIB"),1099511627776,in(available_unit,"P","PB","PI","PIB"),1125899906842624,true(),null())
| eval available_bytes=round(available_number*available_multiplier,0)
| lookup macos_df_capacity_policy.csv host OUTPUT enabled expected_mount warning_used_pct critical_used_pct warning_free_bytes critical_free_bytes owner runbook policy_reviewed
| eval enabled=tonumber(enabled), warning_used_pct=tonumber(warning_used_pct), critical_used_pct=tonumber(critical_used_pct), warning_free_bytes=tonumber(warning_free_bytes), critical_free_bytes=tonumber(critical_free_bytes)
| where enabled=1 AND mounted_on=expected_mount AND used_pct>=0 AND used_pct<=100 AND isnotnull(available_bytes) AND available_bytes>=0 AND warning_used_pct>=0 AND warning_used_pct<critical_used_pct AND critical_used_pct<=100 AND critical_free_bytes>=0 AND critical_free_bytes<warning_free_bytes
| sort 0 host expected_mount -_time
| dedup host expected_mount
| eval sample_age_seconds=round(now()-_time,0)
| where sample_age_seconds>=0 AND sample_age_seconds<=900
| where used_pct>=warning_used_pct OR available_bytes<=warning_free_bytes
| eval severity=if(used_pct>=critical_used_pct OR available_bytes<=critical_free_bytes,"critical","warning"), finding=mvjoin(mvappend(if(used_pct>=warning_used_pct,"used_percentage_threshold",null()),if(available_bytes<=warning_free_bytes,"free_bytes_threshold",null())),";"), free_pct=round(100-used_pct,1), available_gib=round(available_bytes/1073741824,2), use_case="UC-1.1.134"
| table _time host Filesystem Type mounted_on size_display used_display available_display available_bytes available_gib used_pct free_pct warning_used_pct critical_used_pct warning_free_bytes critical_free_bytes severity finding sample_age_seconds policy_reviewed owner runbook use_case
| sort 0 severity -used_pct available_bytes host
description: Reports the newest fresh `Splunk_TA_nix` `df.sh` sample for each policy-enrolled Mac when its exact expected writable mount reaches either a local percentage-used boundary or a local remaining-byte boundary. It preserves the raw command display values, converts only the available-space value with explicit binary units, and rejects wrong-mount, malformed, stale, or invalid-policy data.
value: Low writable space can interrupt macOS updates, application writes, local builds, caches, log collection, swap growth, and user work before a device becomes visibly unusable. Combining a scale-relative percentage with an exact local free-byte reserve gives endpoint teams actionable lead time across differently sized Macs, while explicit APFS and purgeable-space limits prevent the alert from being misrepresented as a whole-container measurement.
implementation: Enable the supplied `df.sh` scripted event input on supported managed Macs at its documented 300-second stanza interval, route it to the local OS event index, and deploy the add-on's search-time knowledge. Build `macos_df_capacity_policy.csv` from the expected Mac inventory with one exact host and writable mount per row; use `/System/Volumes/Data` for a current boot-volume group only after same-host verification. Set percentage and free-byte thresholds from service recovery time, required working headroom, planned update needs, and disk size rather than presenting 90/95 percent or 40/20 GiB as Apple limits. Save the SPL as `macos_filesystem_capacity_from_splunk_ta_df`, run it every five minutes over the delayed window, and operate independent source/policy-health checks.
visualization: Place source and policy health before capacity findings. Show tiles for missing/stale enrolled Macs, invalid or duplicate policy, warnings, and critical findings. Use a newest-first table with host, expected mount, raw available display, exact available GiB, used/free percentage points, both threshold pairs, age, finding, owner, and runbook. Add 24-hour and 30-day lines for `available_bytes` and `used_pct` on separate axes, plus an APFS-aware drilldown showing sibling mount values without summing their used columns. Link to the raw complete `df` event, exact policy row, same-host validation record, and incident. Label `available_gib` as parsed `df` available space, not Finder available, purgeable capacity, total physical-disk free space, or update-ready space.
schema: Splunk_TA_nix df event fields with CIM Performance Storage aliases
dataModelAcceleration: The add-on maps `df` events to CIM Performance/Storage, but the primary detector intentionally uses the raw source type. It must constrain the exact `source=df` feed, preserve raw display fields, enforce a Mac inventory and expected mount, parse the collected unit suffix, select one newest coherent sample, and apply source freshness and local dual thresholds. A generic accelerated Storage dataset can contain non-macOS or other-vendor storage events and CIM defines capacity quantities in megabytes, while historical add-on calculated fields have used byte-oriented conversions. No `cimSpl` is claimed until the installed add-on/CIM versions, object names, units, tags, acceleration coverage, and exact policy behavior are runtime-tested. Acceleration is not required for this five-minute, short-window raw search.

knownFalsePositives:
A finding means the latest qualified sample crossed the configured local policy. The `df` observation can be correct while the operational response is unnecessary or its interpretation is wrong in these cases:

1. **Temporary large download, update staging, build, or media export** — Xcode, software update, package caches, virtual machines, local model artifacts, and video work can consume tens of GiB and release it soon. Confirm the process/workflow owner, recent trend, expected completion, and next samples. Preserve the finding; suppress notification only for an approved bounded job.

2. **APFS snapshots and purgeable-space differences** — Time Machine or update snapshots, clones, caches, and macOS purgeable accounting can make `df`, Disk Utility, Finder, and Storage settings differ. Compare the same host and time, identify which interface reports free versus available/purgeable space, and inspect approved APFS/Time Machine diagnostics. Do not rewrite this `df` result to equal a UI or automatically delete snapshots.

3. **Shared APFS container activity outside the Data volume** — VM, Preboot, Update, Recovery, or another APFS volume can consume shared container space. The Data mount's `Avail` can fall even when its own `Used` value is stable. Treat the free-byte branch as genuine shared-headroom evidence, investigate sibling volumes, and never add sibling `Used` values because APFS sharing, clones, and snapshots make that an invalid total.

4. **Policy does not fit the host's role or disk size** — A 40-GiB reserve can be conservative for a kiosk and insufficient for a developer build host or planned major upgrade. Confirm workload scratch needs, update package requirements, recovery lead time, and disk size. Revise the versioned per-host or cohort policy with owner approval; do not claim the example values are Apple thresholds.

5. **Expected mount changed after migration, reinstall, or older-macOS enrollment** — A host can move between a current APFS volume group and another layout. The primary SPL fails closed on a wrong mount. Compare `/bin/df -h`, Disk Utility with View > Show All Devices, and asset/OS records, then update the exact policy after review. Never broaden the policy to both `/` and `/System/Volumes/Data` merely to restore results.

6. **Duplicate host identity or stale/replayed data** — Cloned forwarder metadata, reused host names, duplicate app deployment, or forwarding replay can associate a valid capacity row with the wrong Mac. Compare forwarder GUID, hardware inventory, `_time`, `_indextime`, raw event, and deployment assignment. Repair identity or collection; do not hide it with long throttling.

7. **Approved capacity or remediation test** — A lab fill test, managed cache purge, or disk-pressure exercise intentionally crosses a threshold. Require the exact host, mount, test owner, ticket, expected boundaries, and UTC start/end. Keep the alert and recovery samples as control evidence.

**Safe suppression:** keep the base detector and source/policy-health searches unchanged. If notification suppression is required, apply a separate post-result lookup keyed by exact `host`, exact `mounted_on`, and use-case ID, with numeric `valid_from_epoch`, exclusive `valid_until_epoch`, owner, approver, ticket, and reason. Reject wildcards, prefixes, open-ended rows, and exceptions for missing/stale/malformed collection or invalid policy. Suppress the action only; retain the result and exception match.
mitreAttack: N/A (operational macOS writable-filesystem capacity monitoring; no adversary behavior is asserted)
hardware: Managed Intel or Apple-silicon Mac systems on a macOS release and Splunk Universal Forwarder/add-on combination qualified by the deployment. Current APFS boot-volume groups normally use `/System/Volumes/Data` as the governed writable mount; external, removable, network, virtual-machine, and non-APFS volumes require separate policy and validation.
reviewer: documentation-only editorial review against Apple df/APFS/storage guidance and Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux, CIM, and scripted-input documentation; collector, lookup, SPL, controls, source health, and dashboard specified but not executed on a Mac or live Splunk platform; no macOS, APFS, Splunk-version, production, or SME sign-off

cost.search_load_notes: One complete tabular df event per managed Mac every five minutes; the alert scans an 18-minute closed window, parses at most the expected mount row per event, applies one small host lookup, and keeps one newest sample per host.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and measurement contract

Assign an endpoint-platform owner, Splunk collection owner, capacity-policy owner, and incident/runbook owner. Install a currently supported Splunk Universal Forwarder and Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux on each managed Mac, and deploy the add-on's parsing and search-time knowledge to the tiers required by the topology. Confirm the installed add-on's compatibility table against every supported macOS and Splunk platform cohort before rollout; this editorial review did not execute a version combination, so the entry makes no `splunkVersions` claim. The forwarder needs its normal outbound receiver route and the privileges required by the supported add-on. Splunk's add-on documentation says it must run as root for the add-on to work properly; review that vendor requirement through endpoint security and do not create broader custom sudo rules. The search role needs read access to the OS index and capacity policy, while lookup write, saved-search edit, and alert-action permissions should be restricted to accountable roles.

Define the measured object before enabling an alert. On current macOS APFS boot-volume groups, the writable user/data volume is normally mounted at `/System/Volumes/Data`, while `/` is the read-only/sealed system side of the group. APFS volumes in one container share free space. Apple explains that the container's free space can be allocated among its volumes; consequently multiple `df` rows can show the same available value while showing different used values. Never add those `Used` columns or describe the Data row's percentage as total physical-disk utilization. An older or nonstandard host may legitimately use `/`, but policy must name one exact expected mount based on same-host evidence.

The base measurement has two independent dimensions. `used_pct` is the percentage printed by `df` for the selected filesystem, normalized from `UsePct`/`Capacity` or the add-on's compatible aliases; it is measured in percentage points from 0 through 100. `available_bytes` is parsed from the raw `Avail` display. `B` means bytes; K/Ki, M/Mi, G/Gi, T/Ti, and P/Pi variants use powers of 1024. An unsuffixed value is treated as one-KiB blocks, matching the add-on's historical conversion contract. The raw human-readable value is rounded by `df`, so derived bytes have the precision of that displayed value and are not an exact block counter. The search does not call `SizeKB`, `UsedKB`, or `AvailKB` because the source does not guarantee fields with those names.

Apple distinguishes free space from available space that can include purgeable files, and user interfaces can present different views. This detector reports the collected `df` semantics only. It does not overwrite them with Finder or Disk Utility values. Use those interfaces as corroborating context and record the difference.

## Step 1 — Configure and qualify `df.sh`

From the installed add-on's `default/inputs.conf`, copy only the supplied `df.sh` stanza into `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/Splunk_TA_nix/local/inputs.conf`; Splunk explicitly warns not to copy the entire default file because local settings persist across upgrades. A conventional override is:

```ini
[script://./bin/df.sh]
interval = 300
sourcetype = df
source = df
index = os
disabled = 0
```

Keep the shipped script and source type unchanged. It is a scripted event input using platform commands including `df`, `mount`, and `fstyp`; it is not HEC, a modular input, or `df_metric.sh`. The documented stanza interval is 300 seconds. One invocation produces one complete tabular event containing a header and rows for mounted filesystems, so event volume is about 288 complete events per Mac per day, not one indexed event per mount. Ensure the add-on's `bin` directory is executable and inspect `splunkd.log` for permission failures. Do not edit `df.sh` to filter rows: changing the header or table can break extraction and removes evidence needed to understand APFS sibling volumes.

Verify effective configuration with `splunk btool inputs list --debug` under the forwarder installation. Search `index=os source=df sourcetype=df earliest=-30m` and inspect `_raw`. Confirm that each event has one header plus complete rows and that the Data row exposes `Filesystem`, `Type`, `Size`, `Used`, `Avail`, `UsePct`, and `MountedOn`. Search-time calculated aliases require the add-on knowledge on the search tier, but the primary SPL uses the documented compatibility/raw fields. Record `_time`, `_indextime`, event size, script duration, and the add-on/macOS/forwarder versions on a representative Intel and Apple-silicon Mac where both are in scope.

Maintain a separate expected-host source-health search. Reconcile the managed-Mac inventory against the latest complete `source=df sourcetype=df` event. Flag no event within two intervals plus measured p95 indexing delay, malformed/missing header, missing expected mount, duplicate current events, script permission or exit errors, unexpected source/index/source type, future timestamps, and host identity collision. Zero capacity findings can never prove that expected Macs reported.

## Step 2 — Create governed mount and threshold policy

Create `macos_df_capacity_policy.csv` with exactly these headers:

```csv
host,enabled,expected_mount,warning_used_pct,critical_used_pct,warning_free_bytes,critical_free_bytes,owner,runbook,policy_reviewed
mac-lab-01,1,/System/Volumes/Data,90,95,42949672960,21474836480,Endpoint Engineering,KB-MAC-CAPACITY,2026-07-28
```

The sample means warning at 90 percentage points used or 40 GiB available, and critical at 95 percentage points or 20 GiB available. It is an example operational policy, not an Apple, APFS, or Splunk recommendation. Set values by device role, disk size, required scratch space, update/rollback plan, time to contact the user, and remediation lead time. A build host may need much more absolute reserve than a kiosk. Keep `0<=warning_used_pct<critical_used_pct<=100` and `0<=critical_free_bytes<warning_free_bytes`; the SPL fails closed on invalid order. Boundaries are inclusive: equality fires.

Use one exact row per Splunk `host`; reject duplicate and wildcard keys. Determine `expected_mount` on the same host with `/bin/df -h /System/Volumes/Data` and Disk Utility's View > Show All Devices. If that path does not exist, establish the writable filesystem deliberately rather than falling back silently to `/`. Set `enabled=0` only for an asset formally out of scope; absence or disablement must remain visible in policy health. Restrict lookup writes, version revisions, validate ISO review dates, and require resolvable owner/runbook values. Reconcile policy hosts to endpoint inventory and raw source health daily.

## Step 3 — Save and understand the capacity search

Save the catalogue SPL as `macos_filesystem_capacity_from_splunk_ta_df`. Schedule it every five minutes, trigger when result count exceeds zero, and preserve the embedded `earliest=-20m@m latest=-2m@m` unless a measured replacement provides the same closed-window and freshness behavior. The two-minute close delay avoids the newest event still being indexed; the 20-minute start gives the search a recent candidate. A result must still be no older than 900 seconds at dispatch. Tune delay and freshness from observed ingestion latency, not by extending them until stale hosts appear healthy.

The base search fixes index, source, source type, and host presence. `mounted_on` accepts the add-on's raw or CIM-compatible mount alias. `used_pct` accepts documented raw/compatibility names, removes only a trailing percent sign, and converts to a number. Raw size/used/available strings are retained for evidence.

`rex` admits only a nonnegative decimal number and a closed binary-display unit vocabulary. The multiplier is explicit: 1 for bytes, 1,024 for KiB, 1,048,576 for MiB, 1,073,741,824 for GiB, and so on. It does not infer `G` as decimal GB. A malformed or unfamiliar suffix leaves `available_bytes` null and is rejected rather than converted to zero. The lookup scopes the feed to enrolled Macs and one exact expected mount. Numeric policy guards reject reversed or out-of-range thresholds.

Sorting and `dedup host,expected_mount` choose one coherent latest row rather than independently combining `latest(Size)`, `latest(Avail)`, and `latest(UsePct)` from different events. Age rejects stale and future samples. The finding condition is OR: either used percentage is high or available bytes are low. Severity is critical if either critical boundary is met; otherwise it is warning. `finding` records which warning-level branches are true. `free_pct=100-used_pct` is the arithmetic complement of this source percentage, not Apple purgeable/available percentage. `available_gib` divides exact parsed bytes by 1,073,741,824 and is labeled GiB.

Do not average APFS sibling percentages, sum sibling used values, or aggregate an unweighted host average. For fleet views count hosts by severity and display distributions of available GiB or used percentage. For trends preserve one mount and both dimensions per host. The base search contains no maintenance exception; suppression belongs after result formation.

## Step 4 — Validate collection, units, thresholds, and APFS meaning

Run the positive and negative `controlTest` variants in an isolated index with fixed event and search times. Validate each gate separately. Assert that `50Gi`, `20Gi`, and `30Gi` produce exactly 53,687,091,200, 21,474,836,480, and 32,212,254,720 bytes. Add suffix tests for `40960Mi`, `40G`, `40GiB`, `41943040K`, and unsuffixed `41943040`; under the documented binary/KiB contract each should represent 40 GiB. Test `40GB` as binary because this parser follows the collector/add-on display convention rather than SI marketing units. Test `40.0Gi`, `0B`, lowercase input, whitespace trimming, malformed suffix, negative number, and scientific notation; unsupported formats must fail closed.

Prove exact threshold behavior. A value at warning used percentage fires warning; one representable value below does not. Equality at critical used percentage is critical. Equality at warning free bytes warns; equality at critical free bytes is critical. If percentage is normal and bytes critical, severity remains critical, and vice versa. Confirm age 900 is accepted and 901 rejected. Insert two valid events for one host and prove only the newer coherent row is evaluated. Confirm a newer malformed row is reported by source health even if the primary search falls back to an older still-fresh valid row.

On each supported macOS/hardware cohort, run `/bin/df -h <expected_mount>` as close as practical to a collector execution. Compare the filesystem, mount, size, used, available, and capacity columns with the indexed raw event and normalized result, allowing only measured collection/forwarding delay and live filesystem change. Compare with the Disk Utility interface: choose View > Show All Devices, select the relevant APFS container and volume, and record its available/purgeable presentation. Also open System Settings > General > Storage. Differences are expected because Apple documents shared APFS free space and available values that can include purgeable content. The test passes when provenance and semantics are explained, not when unrelated interfaces are forced to match.

Validate APFS behavior safely by creating and deleting an ordinary bounded test file on a lab Data volume with ample reserve. Observe Data `Used`, shared `Avail`, the alert fields, and sibling rows before and after. Do not fill a production disk, disable snapshots, delete Time Machine snapshots, alter APFS reserve/quota, or force purgeable reclamation for a control test. Synthetic fixtures prove SPL boundaries; a bounded live file proves collection; neither proves local thresholds are appropriate.

## Step 5 — Operationalize response, evidence, and access

Build the dashboard described in `visualization`, with source/policy health first. Keep raw display values beside normalized values and show both threshold branches. A responder should first verify source freshness, expected mount, policy revision, and exact branch. Then compare current `/bin/df -h`, Disk Utility/APFS hierarchy, and Storage settings; inspect 24-hour and 30-day trends; review software-update staging, Xcode/build artifacts, media, virtual machines, local backups/snapshots, caches, logs, Trash, and user workflow through approved tools; and identify whether shared-container activity rather than Data growth reduced available space.

Warning should normally create an endpoint-capacity work item. Critical routing depends on role and impact: a CI Mac or shared service may page sooner than a user workstation. Deduplicate notification by exact host, expected mount, and severity for no longer than one collection interval unless the incident system separately tracks escalation. A critical transition must reopen or escalate. Do not automatically delete files, purge caches, thin snapshots, empty Trash, remove user data, uninstall software, resize APFS volumes, or restart a Mac from this result. Follow an owner-approved cleanup or storage runbook and preserve before/after evidence.

Restrict raw host/storage events and device-to-user joins to endpoint/platform roles. The capacity values are not highly sensitive alone, but host identity, installed workflow, file categories, and incident notes can expose user or project context. Retain raw events and result artifacts according to local operations policy; the 30-day cost estimate is not a mandated retention period. Keep `status=draft` until the collector, fields, policy, source health, unit fixtures, APFS comparisons, alert actions, dashboard, RBAC, and response runbook are executed and signed off on every supported cohort.

## Step 6 — Troubleshoot without changing semantics

- **No `df` events:** verify add-on assignment, enabled local stanza, executable `bin` directory, effective `btool` output, forwarder output route, target index, and `ExecProcessor`/permission messages in `splunkd.log`. This source does not use HEC or a vendor API.
- **Raw event exists but mount fields are null:** inspect whether the event retained its header and complete table, verify `sourcetype=df`, and deploy the matching add-on search-time knowledge. A pipeline that removes or changes columns must preserve the source-type contract or use a separately qualified source type.
- **Mac has data but no primary result:** inspect the policy row, exact case-sensitive `host`, `enabled`, expected mount, threshold order, newest sample age, percentage, and available suffix. Use a separate diagnostic search before weakening any gate.
- **Only `/` appears on a current Mac:** compare the raw complete event with `/bin/df -h` and verify the installed script/add-on/macOS support matrix. Do not change policy to `/` until the writable-volume layout is proven; a missing Data row is source health.
- **`available_bytes` is null:** inspect the exact `Avail` token. Confirm it is a documented output of the installed collector and update paired fixtures before extending the parser. Never remove letters generically or turn parse failure into zero, because either can create false critical pages.
- **Byte value differs by about 7 percent:** an operator probably compared binary GiB with decimal GB. This search uses powers of 1024 and labels the output GiB. Compare bytes first.
- **Percentage differs from `100*Used/Size`:** macOS `df` documents capacity in relation to used plus available for the filesystem, and APFS shares available space. Trust the collected percentage field under its documented semantics; do not recompute it from rounded human-readable Size/Used values.
- **Finder or Disk Utility shows more available:** determine whether the interface includes purgeable space. Keep both observations with labels. Do not add purgeable space to `df` automatically or silence the rule solely because a UI is more optimistic.
- **Repeated warning after deleting files:** snapshots, clones, open files, caches, or sibling-volume activity can retain blocks or shared pressure. Recheck current command output and approved APFS diagnostics; do not automate snapshot deletion.
- **Duplicate or wrong-host results:** inspect duplicate input stanzas, relays, cloned `host` metadata, forwarder GUIDs, and replay. Repair collection identity rather than adding broad `dedup` or exceptions.
- **CIM/tstats result disagrees:** compare installed CIM/add-on versions, tag constraints, object hierarchy, acceleration range, field units, source mix, and mount aliases. The raw detector is authoritative for this UC until an accelerated variant passes the same Mac scope, exact unit, freshness, policy, and boundary controls.
grandmaExplanation: We watch the writable part of each Mac's main storage and warn when it is either too full or has too little working room left. This gives the support team time to help before updates or everyday work start failing.
